assessment.nobel_worthiness: Bayesian persuasion and information design supplied a highly generative framework for strategic disclosure, with influence across theory and applied market settings.
assessment.attribution: Bergemann and Kamenica are the clearest central originators; the broader credited group reflects important extensions and adjacent foundations.
assessment.maturity: The framework is well established, widely used, and sufficiently mature for a prize.
uncertainties: The appropriate boundary between the original persuasion contribution and the wider information-design literature remains contestable.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Dynamic discrete choice made forward-looking structural analysis operational across labour, industrial organization, and related fields.
assessment.attribution: Rust is indispensable to the foundational computational and econometric breakthrough, while Keane and Eckstein represent major development and application of the approach.
assessment.maturity: Its methods have endured for decades and produced a large, demonstrable research program.
uncertainties: Credit is diffuse because subsequent methodological advances involve many contributors outside the proposed trio.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Alternating-offer bargaining and bargaining-in-markets models transformed analysis of strategic negotiation and decentralized trade.
assessment.attribution: Rubinstein is the unmistakable anchor for alternating-offers theory; Wolinsky and Binmore capture major market and bargaining contributions.
assessment.maturity: The contribution is exceptionally mature and remains a basic reference point in game theory.
uncertainties: The unifying case across bilateral bargaining and market bargaining may be broader than a single sharply delimited discovery.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Economic network theory gave rigorous tools for social learning, strategic links, and networked interaction with broad relevance.
assessment.attribution: Jackson, Kranton, and Goyal each made central, complementary contributions to the listed network agenda.
assessment.maturity: The area has accumulated a deep theoretical canon and extensive applications.
uncertainties: The field spans several distinct literatures, making a compact and exclusive attribution difficult.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Models of ambiguity supplied durable alternatives to subjective expected utility and reshaped theoretical work on decisions under uncertainty.
assessment.attribution: Gilboa and Epstein are central to the respective maxmin and recursive-ambiguity foundations; Marinacci represents substantial related work.
assessment.maturity: The theories are long established and have generated extensive work in decision theory, finance, and macroeconomics.
uncertainties: The intellectual case combines distinct ambiguity frameworks rather than one indivisible result.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Firm heterogeneity and selection fundamentally changed modern trade theory and empirical interpretation of trade gains.
assessment.attribution: Melitz is central to the canonical heterogeneous-firm model, with Helpman and Redding making major complementary theoretical contributions.
assessment.maturity: The framework is firmly embedded in trade research and policy analysis.
uncertainties: The large subsequent literature makes the boundary between foundational and follow-on credit difficult to draw.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Quantile regression created a foundational way to study heterogeneous conditional distributions rather than only conditional means.
assessment.attribution: Koenker and Bassett are the defining originators; Chernozhukov represents important later distributional econometrics.
assessment.maturity: The method has had decades of sustained theoretical, empirical, and cross-disciplinary use.
uncertainties: Whether methodological breadth alone is sufficiently prize-defining relative to other econometric advances is a judgment call.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Work on insurance selection connected economic theory, credible measurement, and consequential evidence on health and credit insurance markets.
assessment.attribution: Finkelstein, Einav, and Salanie represent complementary empirical and theoretical contributions to the stated agenda.
assessment.maturity: The literature is mature and its empirical designs have influenced applied public economics.
uncertainties: Attribution across the broader adverse-selection literature is unusually expansive.
